impact_assessment.why: The user asked to continue photo-harbor; after accounts and folders, the library has no way to collect a subset of photos or mark keepers across months
impact_assessment.benefits: Personal albums and favorites with no file moves; plain-folder layout untouched; favorites and albums stay private per person; additive migration keeps existing libraries
impact_assessment.risks: contract: catalog format 5 and new API fields; dependency: none (sqlite3 only); concurrency: album writes share the database lock with scans and uploads; state: v4->v5 migration and album rows
impact_assessment.mitigation: Additive CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS only, no row rewrites; the existing .v4.bak backs the upgrade; every album and favorite query is scoped to the signed-in profile; tests cover migration, privacy, add/remove and paging

[1/5] Plan: gallery Select mode with checkmarked tiles, a selection bar (count, select all loaded, favorite/unfavorite, add to album, clear, done); bulk /api/favorite and /api/album-photos accept sha256s up to 500, validate every hash before writing, and apply in one lock; tests, dogfood, ADR-011, README

impact_assessment.why: Albums work, but adding a trip's photos one viewer at a time is tedious; bulk selection is the missing step between browsing and collecting
impact_assessment.benefits: Collect dozens of photos in two clicks; fewer requests and one database lock per batch; no schema change and no file moves
impact_assessment.risks: contract: /api/favorite and /api/album-photos gain a sha256s form; dependency: none; concurrency: bulk writes hold the catalog lock; state: selection is client-only and resets on filter changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: Cap batches at 500, pre-validate existence and ownership before any write, keep single-sha requests working, and test partial-failure refusal plus cross-person refusal
